newsitem.title: UK: Crude tanker rates for 80kt ships slip in UK/Cont.
newsitem.headline: Crude tanker rates for 80kt ships slip in UK/Cont.

text.p: Chartering rates for 80,000 tonne crude oil tankers making journeys within northwestern Europe eased on Tuesday from recent sky-high levels and brokers said they expected a further erosion of rates.
Three fixtures at W140 were indicative of falling rates from levels as high as W155 on Friday.
"Today rates are down to the 140-145 level and I think it will come off, for early June liftings, down to around W120," one said.
He added that a number of current stems had disappeared on larger ships and this had eased the pressure on Aframaxes.
Med rates for similarly sized vessels were steady to slightly firmer amid healthy enquiry. Brokers assessed levels at around W105-107.5, slightly firmer than last week.

Mideast/Asia and Mideast/West routes were steady at current levels, with fresh Mideast/Japan business seen done for 250,000 tonners at W65 and KPC's fixture of the 285,000 tonne Equatorial Lion at W53.5 from the Mideast to the west seen broadly in line with last week's levels.

Rates for fuel oil vessels in Europe were steady with few stems seeking ships in May but a dearth of 25,000 tonners also. Rates for 25,000 tonners in the Med were assessed at around W195 while in the UK/Cont region they were seen closer to W210.
